newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai cabinet allows issue of government bonds.
newsitem.headline: Thai cabinet allows issue of government bonds.

text.p: The Thai cabinet on Tuesday approved amended legislation that will allow the government to issue bonds even though the country does not face a budget deficit, Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said.

He told reporters the move was aimed at helping create a benchmark in the country's fledgling secondary bond market and proceeds from the issues would be used to re-lend to state agencies to finance infrastructure projects.

The amount of domestic government bonds to be issued each fiscal year must not exceed 10 percent of approved spending, he said. After the green light from the cabinet, the draft of the amended legislation would be placed in parliament.
Amnuay told Reuters earlier that the government would push for the legislation in order to be able to issue the bonds within this year.
Current Thai laws prohibit the government from issuing bonds locally unless it is to finance a fiscal deficit -- which Thailand has had for the past decade.

However, during the first three months of fiscal 1996/97 (October-September), the government ran a budget deficit of 53.76 billion baht due to a jump in budget reimbursement and lower-than-expected revenues collection.

But Amnuay insisted that the budget this year would be balanced and the government would cut unneceesary spending. He has said more than 50 billion baht, in what was viewed as unnecessary spending, would be slashed this fiscal year.
The idea was not to use the money to finance a deficit as Thailand had big fiscal reserves but to create depth in the debt market, Amnuay said.
